title: Temporary access code serves as identifier
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest user can serve as a unique reference to identify that specific guest's access attempt to the home hub.
assumptions: The access code is logged and associated with the guest user's identity or access event.

title: Sensitive access code data collected
description: The temporary access code is sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required for the functional goal of unlocking the door.
assumptions: The access code contains information that could be used to identify or track the guest user.

title: Access code retention beyond functional need
description: The temporary access code may be stored longer than functionally needed for the door unlocking operation, creating unnecessary privacy risk.
assumptions: The system logs access codes for audit or security purposes beyond the immediate access event.

title: Guest unaware of data processing
description: The guest user may not be fully aware that their temporary access code is being collected, processed, and potentially stored by the home hub system.
assumptions: No clear consent or notification mechanism is provided to the guest about data collection practices.

title: Guest lacks control over data processing preferences
description: The guest user has limited ability to set preferences or control how their access code data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: The system does not provide options for the guest to opt-out of data collection or control data retention.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data (access code) than is actually needed to achieve the functional goal of unlocking the front door.
assumptions: Alternative authentication methods that don't require storing the access code could be used.

title: Sensitive motion data collected beyond functional necessity
description: Real-time motion alerts may contain more sensitive personal data than strictly required for the home security functionality. Motion data can reveal patterns of life, presence, and behavior that exceed basic security monitoring needs.

title: Data propagation to mobile backend beyond necessity
description: Motion alert data is propagated from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend where it may be accessible by parties beyond the immediate functional requirement of the security system.

title: Data subject unawareness of motion data processing
description: Home users may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, transmitted, and processed by the backend system, particularly if this occurs as part of automated security monitoring.

title: Lack of user control over motion data preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their motion data is processed, stored, and shared with the mobile app backend.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing motion data that may be more granular than functionally required could violate GDPR data minimization principles, as the system may collect and process more personal data than necessary for security monitoring.

title: Data accessible to predetermined set of parties
description: Motion alert data at the Mobile App Backend may be accessible to a predetermined set of parties (e.g., app developers, analytics services) beyond the immediate functional need.

title: Revealing attributes in motion data
description: Motion alert data may contain revealing attributes (e.g., time of day, location, activity patterns) that support identification of the data subject through behavioral analysis.

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The video clip stored in the cloud is identified data associated with a specific homeowner, and is being retrieved and processed by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: The video is linked to a specific homeowner identity in the system.

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content may reveal personal attributes about the homeowner (e.g., location, activities, possessions) that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Video content contains observable personal information about the homeowner.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be perceived as more sensitive than strictly required for playback functionality.
assumptions: Video content is inherently sensitive and may contain more detail than needed for simple playback.

title: Potential unnecessary video processing
description: The video may be processed, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is functionally needed for simple playback (e.g., metadata extraction, content analysis).
assumptions: The system may perform additional processing on the video beyond playback.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if additional processing occurs beyond playback.

title: Homeowner unawareness of video processing
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of how their video data is being processed, stored, or potentially disclosed by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not fully explain all processing activities.

title: Lack of homeowner control over video processing
description: The homeowner may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular consent controls for video data.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the playback functionality, violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR applies to this system and video processing may exceed functional necessity.
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual system design and data minimization practices.

title: Video data accessible to more parties than needed
description: The video data retrieved by the mobile app backend may be accessible to more parties (e.g., other services, third parties) than functionally necessary for playback.
assumptions: The backend may share or propagate video data to other systems.
uncertainty_note: Depends on backend architecture and data sharing policies.

title: Lack of homeowner access to video data
description: The homeowner may lack control in accessing the personal video data that is being processed by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: The system may not provide adequate access controls for the data subject.
